title.narrative: Output 1.1. Increased institutional capacity of employer and business membership organizations (EBMOs)

description.narrative: The Federation of Kenya Employers (FKE) adapted its strategy and internal processes to adjust to a changing business environment and address members’ training needs. The COVID-19 pandemic greatly disrupted FKE’s training outputs pushing it to adapt to online and blended training options. FKE created a new online training platform that enabled the organization to provide training online and widen its reach to member enterprises beyond metropolitan areas with FKE offices. In July 2022, FKE launched a national Report “The Next Normal: How Kenya’s workplace is changing” which identified new areas for training. Recognizing an opportunity to align with evolving regulator measures for companies, FKE introduced Environmental Social and Governance (ESG) training. This new ESG training was offered in a blended approach using FKE’s new online training platform. To assess the market, an online sensitization seminar was conducted in July 2022, attracting 300 members, including 15 CEOs. FKE then followed this up with a targeted pilot training in Oct with 25 member companies. FKE collaborated with the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE) as a training partner. In advance of the initial pilot ESG training, FKE deployed a new ESG survey tool (Leader Pulse-check) to gather baseline data. Two FKE board member companies were part of this pilot testing and they subsequently confirmed at FKE board level its importance. A separate deep dive analysis was conducted alongside this training through a clinic for 12 FKE members in Oct 2022, further refining the ESG training. The initial commercially run ESG training took place in June-July of 2023 with 82 member companies participating proving the financial sustainability of the training. The cost of these trainings is US$480 for members and US$685 non-members. FKE produced and published a member briefing on ESG trends in Kenya to further promote the training, along with a separate flyer promotional flyer for the training. The ILO in partnership with ITC-ILO provided technical support to FKE in the development of its new online training platform. Specifically, the ILO trained 5 umber of FKE staff members on effectively operating and maintaining the platform. This training occurred over 7 online sessions from May to July 2023 and a final physical training held in Kigali in Sept 2023. The ILO provided FKE with support to draft its national Report “The Next Normal: How Kenya’s workplace is changing” by identifying significant shifts in Kenya’s workplace relations and labour law, skills development and productivity, and overall human resources. Furthermore, the ILO provided FKE with support to test the market for new ESG training through an online sensitization seminar in July 2022. Subsequently, the ILO supported FKE in running a targeted pilot training (physical) in Oct 2022. The ILO additionally supported a separate ESG clinic for FKE members. The ILO provided further training on ESG for 4 FKE trainers (Kigali, Sept 2023). The ILO provided FKE with technical speakers as they launched the first commercially run ESG training (19-23 June 2023). The ILO supported FKE in developing material for this training course including a new Leader Pulse-check training tool. The ILO also supported FKE in the development of a FKE member brief on ESG and a promotional flyer, both of which were used to promote the new training. The ILO supported FKE in developing a FKE policy framework on Migration within a Kenyan context (June 2022) which was important base material for FKEs ESG training.
